To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal regulation of a foreign-invested firm under external credit constraint is characterized by: (1) a discontinuous production profile, and (2) a maximum profit constraint for the regulated firm.
A credit-constrained country that wants to send profits to foreign investors has to generate a sufficient trade surplus to compensate for capital outflows.
In a credit constrained economy, the government has to choose a regulatory policy that is not efficient in order to maintain incentive compatibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between optimal regulation and credit constraints.
a theoretical and empirical analysis of the interaction between optimal regulation, external capital flows and exchange rate policy.
the interactions of external credit constraints and regulation in a small open economy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal regulatory policy is not necessarily to maximize social welfare, as it is the case under perfect capital mobility.
a country with a credit constraint should not be too quick in liberalizing foreign investments.

the optimal regulation of a foreign-owned firm is not necessarily less stringent when the credit-constrained economy wants to send abroad the profits generated by the foreign investment, as long as the economy has access to a foreign currency exchange rate policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the external credit constraint is an important factor to consider in the analysis of the optimal regulation.
the credit constraint may have an important role to play in determining the level of efficiency in the regulated industry.
the optimal regulation is a function of the credit constraint.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the credit constraint is not only relevant for the firm, but it is also relevant for the government and for the economy as a whole.
the optimal regulation of a credit-constrained economy is not necessarily the same as the optimal regulation in a non-credit constrained economy.
the optimal regulatory policy in a credit-constrained developing country is different from the one in a developed country.
